Israel's election -- seen as a referendum on Benjamin Netanyahu's national security strategy -- appears to have thrown up a hung verdict with neither Bibi nor his challenger Gadi Eisenkot securing a clear majority. In this situation, the Arab parties have emerged as potential kingmakers. However, their role in government formation remains uncertain.
In episode 1927 of , ThePrint Editor-in-Chief Shekhar Gupta examines the results, the coalition arithmetic and what the outcome could mean for Israel’s wars and future. ThePrint Editor (Operations) Janki Dave joins from Jerusalem.
